title: My Knee X-Ray Shows Arthritis (Grade 3 or 4, "Bone on Bone"): What Does It Mean?
metaDescription: X-ray says knee arthritis or 'bone on bone'? The amount of damage on an X-ray does not decide your pain or whether you need surgery. Here is why.
intro: An X-ray showing arthritis does not mean you need an operation. The amount of damage on an X-ray does not reliably predict how much pain you have. Some people with severe-looking X-rays have little pain, and some with mild X-rays have a lot. Treatment is based on you, not on the picture.

sections.heading: Does 'bone on bone' mean I need a knee replacement?
sections.body: Not automatically. 'Bone on bone' describes what the X-ray shows. The decision depends on your pain, your walking, your sleep and your daily life, and on whether other treatments have helped. Many people with advanced X-ray changes manage well for a long time.

sections.heading: Why doesn't my X-ray match my pain?
sections.body: Versus Arthritis says the amount of joint damage does not reliably predict pain. Muscle strength, weight, sleep, mood and activity all affect how much a knee hurts. That is why we examine you and ask about your life, not only the film.

sections.heading: What are the grades on a knee X-ray?
sections.body: Reports often use grades from 1 to 4, from mild to severe. A higher grade means more visible change. It helps your doctor, but it is only one piece of information.

sections.heading: Do I need blood tests or an MRI?
sections.body: There is no blood test that diagnoses knee arthritis, although blood tests are sometimes done to rule out other conditions. Your doctor decides whether any other scan is needed for your particular knee.

sections.heading: When does the X-ray matter?
sections.body: If surgery is being considered, standing X-rays help plan it and check which parts of the knee are affected. That decides whether a partial or total knee replacement is suitable.

sections.heading: What should I do next?
sections.body: Treat the symptoms first. We usually start with medicines, then exercises, then physiotherapy treatments and an injection if needed. If pain still limits your life, we talk about surgery. You decide.

faqs.q: What does grade 4 knee arthritis mean?
faqs.a: It means the X-ray shows advanced change. It does not by itself decide treatment.

faqs.q: Can I avoid knee replacement with severe arthritis on X-ray?
faqs.a: Many people do, if pain is controllable with other treatment.

faqs.q: Is an MRI needed for knee arthritis?
faqs.a: Not usually to diagnose arthritis. It may be used if an injury such as a torn meniscus is suspected.
